title: Count Basie offers $35 a week; later she joins and meets John Hammond
summary: Basie heard her at the Cotton Club and offered $35 a week to replace Billie Holiday. She declined, then later travelled with his band to New York, where she sang at the Renaissance Ballroom and John Hammond heard her.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well anyway, that's where I was working when the Basie Band played in town. And after their gig, well they came, you know, to the Cotton Club and Basie heard me and he told me when he was talking to me, and he said, 'well I certainly enjoyed your singing'. He said, 'I'd like to have you come and sing with my band'. I said, 'yeah, who is your band?' He said, 'I'm sorry, I didn't introduce myself. I'm Count Basie'. I said, 'oh, well.' I said, 'well, how much do you pay?' He said, 'I pay $35 a week'. I said, 'Oh, no. I make $35 a week here and I don't have to go no place. I don't have to travel'. He said, 'well, we were trying to find somebody to take Billie Holiday's place and we enjoy you'. I said, 'well thank you so much, but right now I'll just stay here'. So I didn't go. But then later on during the year I decided to travel with his band and I went with

him and ended up in New York. I started working for Androde at the Renaissance Ballroom. And so Mr. Androde asked Al if he could get me to come and sing on some special night it was. But they were having a big ball there and John Hammond was in the party. He came to this big reception and all this, and John Hammond was there and he heard me. And so then he went back and talked with Al, you know, about me going for some recordings and getting with the Basie Band. So that was the first time I met John, was then. He enjoyed me so much, he wanted to put me right with the band. So anyway, I made my first session when I got to New York with Harry James.
